stages.text:
Red Kidney Bean: Seed to Seedling
kind: explainer
style: Live-action macro realism with simple growth animation, a fixed widescreen camera, and overhead illumination.
In the opening two seconds, a fixed widescreen live-action close-up shows a dry red kidney bean planted in perlite, its hard coat and hilum visible. Simple animation compresses the documented growth sequence: the bean absorbs water, swells, and its coat progressively loosens rather than disappearing. The voice-over begins: “A seed takes in water.”

From seconds two to five, the radicle emerges and extends downward in response to gravity; lateral roots begin forming as the cotyledons swell. The first leaves remain within the loosening coat before beginning to appear alongside the cotyledons. The narration continues: “Roots grow downward, and a shoot reaches up toward the light.”

In the final three seconds, the first leaves push upward past the cotyledons on an upright stem beneath overhead illumination. The two unifoliate leaves unfold and expand, revealing the terminal growing tip, with the developing root system visible below. The sequence ends on this young seedling, without on-screen text or music.
stages.note: research: One documented botanical episode: a red kidney bean developing from a dry seed into a rooted seedling, based on the University of Nebraska–Lincoln Plant & Soil Sciences eLibrary’s day-by-day photographic sequence. The source gives days after planting, not calendar dates or a confirmed filming location. Compress approximately 12 days into an 8-second, widescreen animation; do not imply real-time growth. Suggested staging: 0–2 seconds, water uptake and swelling; 2–5 seconds, root emergence and downward growth; 5–8 seconds, shoot rising toward overhead light. Exact voice-over: “A seed takes in water. Roots grow downward, and a shoot reaches up toward the light.” No on-screen text or music.

stages.text:
Coffee, Yes; Stimulus, No
kind: short
style: Live-action video podcast for YouTube, 16:9; natural textures, warm studio lighting, and a gentle camera push that keeps both hosts on screen.
In Cedar Studio, warm lamplight falls across a walnut table. Maya sits on the left behind Maya’s microphone; Leo sits on the right behind Leo’s microphone. A bookshelf and soft amber curtains fill the background. Both hosts remain visible in a wide shot. On-screen labels identify Maya as “Keynesian economist” and Leo as “Austrian-school economist.”

Maya leans toward Maya’s microphone. “In a recession, government should spend to restore demand and get people working.”

Leo raises an open hand beside Leo’s microphone. “But spending and cheap money fuel the boom that leads to the bust.”

The camera eases closer, keeping both hosts and both microphones in frame. Maya tilts Maya’s coffee mug toward Leo and smiles. “Then we disagree on stimulus, not on having another coffee.”

Leo lifts Leo’s coffee mug toward Maya’s coffee mug, smiling back. “Coffee, yes; stimulus, no—let the economy correct itself.”

stages.text:
Citric acid cycle
kind: explainer
style: 60-second widescreen explainer in simple, clean 2D animation using textbook-style diagrams; calm English narration; no music.
Under “Citric acid cycle,” an oval mitochondrial cutaway shows a symbolic, arrow-linked loop in the matrix. Labels identify molecules as calm English narration follows the reactions. Acetyl-CoA supplies a two-carbon acetyl group to four-carbon oxaloacetate, forming six-carbon citrate; CoA-SH is released.

Citrate rearranges into six-carbon isocitrate. Isocitrate becomes five-carbon α-ketoglutarate: CO₂ leaves and the first NADH appears. Next, four-carbon succinyl-CoA forms, releasing a second CO₂ and producing a second NADH. The departing carbons are not the newly arrived acetyl carbons.

Succinyl-CoA becomes succinate, releasing CoA-SH; a GTP → ATP callout represents one ATP equivalent, not two additional products. Membrane-embedded succinate dehydrogenase converts succinate to fumarate as FAD becomes FADH₂. Water enters as fumarate becomes malate.

Malate becomes oxaloacetate, producing the third NADH. The regenerated oxaloacetate can accept another acetyl group, closing the loop. The completed turn shows two CO₂, three NADH, one FADH₂ and one ATP equivalent.
stages.note: research: Citric acid cycle — research for one complete turn inside a mitochondrion, rather than a historical discovery episode. Follow acetyl-group entry, energy capture, carbon dioxide release and oxaloacetate regeneration. Dates below identify source publication dates, not dates when these recurring biochemical reactions occurred. The 60-second running time is a presentation choice, not the measured duration of one turn.

params.prompt:
Create a 60-second educational explainer for first-year university biology students. Widescreen 16:9. Simple clean flat 2D vector animation, white background, dark high-contrast readable text, uncluttered diagram, restrained teal blue orange palette. Fixed camera, no photorealism, no cuts away from the educational diagram. AUDIO: calm clear English adult narrator speaking the timed script below, synchronized with diagram highlights. Absolutely NO music, no soundtrack, no sound effects. Persistent exact title at top: 'Citric acid cycle'. Show a cutaway mitochondrion, identifiable outer membrane and folded inner membrane, with the large reaction loop INSIDE the mitochondrial MATRIX. Clearly label 'Matrix'. Lay out eight reaction nodes clockwise in a large readable loop with directional arrows. Reveal and retain molecule names as they appear. Main loop labels in order: Oxaloacetate (4C), Citrate (6C), Isocitrate (6C), alpha-Ketoglutarate (5C), Succinyl-CoA (4C), Succinate (4C), Fumarate (4C), Malate (4C), then return to Oxaloacetate (4C). Keep labels accurate and legible, no invented words. One process, one continuous coherent infographic.
TIMELINE, VISUALS AND EXACT NARRATION:
0-6 seconds: Reveal mitochondrion and loop in its matrix. Narrator: 'The citric acid cycle takes place in the mitochondrial matrix. It captures energy from acetyl-CoA.'
6-14 seconds: A labeled Acetyl-CoA (2C) arrow enters and joins Oxaloacetate (4C), generating Citrate (6C); show CoA leaving. Narrator: 'A two-carbon acetyl group joins four-carbon oxaloacetate, forming six-carbon citrate. Coenzyme A is released.'
14-19 seconds: Highlight Citrate to Isocitrate, retain six carbon count. Narrator: 'Citrate rearranges into isocitrate, preparing it for the next reactions.'
19-27 seconds: Highlight Isocitrate to alpha-Ketoglutarate, show one CO2 exiting and NAD+ changing to NADH beside this arrow. Narrator: 'Isocitrate loses carbon dioxide and forms alpha-ketoglutarate. Energy is captured as NADH.'
27-35 seconds: Highlight alpha-Ketoglutarate to Succinyl-CoA, show second separate CO2 leaving and another NAD+ changing to NADH. Narrator: 'Another carbon dioxide leaves as succinyl-CoA forms, producing a second NADH.'
35-42 seconds: Highlight Succinyl-CoA to Succinate, CoA leaves and ADP plus phosphate produces ATP, with small note 'via GTP in many cells'. Narrator: 'Succinyl-CoA becomes succinate. This step produces ATP, or GTP that can transfer its energy to ATP.'
42-48 seconds: Highlight Succinate to Fumarate, FAD changes to FADH2. Narrator: 'Succinate becomes fumarate, transferring energy to FAD to make FADH2.'
48-54 seconds: Highlight Fumarate to Malate, small H2O entry arrow; then Malate to Oxaloacetate with NAD+ to NADH. Narrator: 'Water helps form malate. Malate then regenerates oxaloacetate and produces a third NADH.'
54-60 seconds: Complete the loop highlight and briefly pulse the incoming acetyl-CoA arrow. Show summary panel 'Per acetyl-CoA: 2 CO2 | 3 NADH | 1 FADH2 | 1 ATP or GTP'. Narrator: 'Oxaloacetate is ready again. Each turn yields two carbon dioxide, three NADH, one FADH2, and one ATP equivalent.'
SCIENTIFIC ACCURACY: Exactly two carbon dioxide exits, at isocitrate oxidation and alpha-ketoglutarate oxidation. Do not imply the two incoming acetyl carbons necessarily leave as CO2 on their first turn. Exactly three NADH production sites, one FADH2 production site, one ATP-equivalent site. Oxygen is not consumed directly by this loop. Do not depict the electron transport chain. All labels lie under the persistent title. Calm measured narration with enough time for all spoken lines; no extra speech.
